subject: chemistry
chapter_title: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques

concepts.title: Tetravalence of Carbon, Structural Representations and Classification
concepts.definition: Carbon's tetravalency and catenation build a vast organic chemistry, whose compounds are classified as acyclic, alicyclic, aromatic and heterocyclic, and are represented by complete, condensed and bond line structural formulas with three dimensional wedge dash notation.
concepts.key_idea: Functional groups and multiple bonds decide the class of an organic compound, and the classification tree separates open chain from cyclic structures.
question_patterns: explain tetravalence and catenation of carbon
differentiate complete condensed and bond line formulas
what are homocyclic and heterocyclic compounds
draw the wedge dash representation of a molecule

solution_steps.explain: Identify the carbon framework from the formula.
Note cyclic parts and characteristic groups.
Assign acyclic, alicyclic, aromatic or heterocyclic class.

concepts.title: IUPAC Nomenclature of Organic Compounds
concepts.definition: IUPAC nomenclature names an organic compound from a parent hydrocarbon, numbered substituents and functional groups with lowest locants, using prefixes, word root and suffix, so that each structure has one unambiguous name and each name defines one structure.
concepts.key_idea: The longest chain carrying the highest priority functional group becomes the parent, and alphabetical order handles multiple substituents.
question_patterns: state the rules of iupac nomenclature of organic compounds
name branched alkanes by the iupac system
how are functional groups ordered in naming priority
write the iupac name from a given structure
define locant and its use in nomenclature
name alkenes alkynes and substituted benzene compounds

solution_steps.explain: Choose the longest chain with the senior functional group.
Number from the end nearest the functional group.
Place prefixes alphabetically before the root and suffix.

concepts.title: Isomerism, Fission of Bonds and Reaction Intermediates
concepts.definition: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different properties are isomers, showing structural isomerism of chain, position and functional types; covalent bonds break by homolytic fission giving free radicals or heterolytic fission giving cations and anions, and electron displacement effects of inductive, resonance, electromeric and hyperconjugation govern organic reactions.
concepts.key_idea: Nucleophiles donate electron pairs to electrophiles, and carbocations, carbanions and free radicals are the fleeting intermediates of organic reactions.
question_patterns: define isomerism and its structural types with examples
differentiate homolytic and heterolytic fission of a covalent bond
explain inductive effect and resonance effect
what are electrophiles and nucleophiles with examples
describe carbocations carbanions and free radicals as intermediates

solution_steps.explain: Confirm isomers share the molecular formula.
Note whether bonding electrons are shared or transferred.
Name the species or displacement effect governing the reaction.
